N-2.1-A.skill: relate the average rate of change over an interval to the instantaneous rate for a quadratic position function, solving for the time.

N-2.1-B.skill: decide what a net change over an interval does and does not tell you: average rate, not instantaneous rate or constant rate.

N-2.2-A.skill: identify the function and point behind a difference-quotient limit and evaluate it as a derivative.

N-2.2-B.skill: find the error in a limit-definition derivation where f(x + h) is expanded incorrectly, and state the correct derivative.

N-2.3-A.skill: estimate acceleration from a table of velocity values with uneven spacing, then use the signs of velocity and acceleration to decide whether the object is speeding up.

N-2.3-B.skill: use the monotonic behaviour of f′ to bracket f′(a) between the slopes of secant lines on either side of a.

N-2.4-A.skill: choose constants that make a piecewise function both continuous and differentiable at the join, using the slopes and values of both pieces.

N-2.4-B.skill: count the points where the absolute value of a polynomial fails to be differentiable by telling simple roots from repeated roots.

N-2.5-A.skill: find the points of tangency of lines drawn from an external point to a power-function curve.

N-2.5-B.skill: use the power rule to find where a rate of change numerically equals the quantity itself in a geometric context.

N-2.6-A.skill: use the fact that a constant term disappears under differentiation to choose the constant that makes a horizontal line tangent.

N-2.6-B.skill: work backward from a given derivative of a combination to the derivative of a component function, using the sum and constant multiple rules.

N-2.7-A.skill: find where a tangent line to e^x or ln x passes through a given external point.

N-2.7-B.skill: differentiate a sum that contains constant-valued exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric terms without treating the constants as variables.

N-2.8-A.skill: use the product rule backward: a horizontal tangent to a product determines the derivative of one factor.

N-2.8-B.skill: apply the product rule to a rate in context, such as revenue as price times quantity, and interpret the result with units.

N-2.9-A.skill: use the quotient rule backward: a horizontal tangent to a quotient determines a derivative of the numerator.

N-2.9-B.skill: use the quotient rule on an average-cost function to find where average cost stops falling.

N-2.10-A.skill: solve for the points where the tangent to tan x or cot x has a given slope, using sec²x and csc²x and keeping both solutions in the interval.

N-2.10-B.skill: combine derivative formulas and identities to determine the sign of a derivative and describe monotonic behaviour.
